content: Certainly. 1. Estrogens, when administered in high systemic doses, may reduce tissue sensitivity to the action of hyaluronidase. Patients may require higher doses of hyaluronidase to achieve the same dispersing effect. 2. Idelalisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Idelalisib is a strong CYP3A inhibitor and should not be used with sensitive CYP3A substrates. 3. Iloperidone increases ethinyl estradiol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Iloperidone is a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor and may elevate plasma levels of drugs primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. 4. Ethinyl estradiol may reduce the oxidative metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing serum concentrations and the risk of TCA-related adverse effects. 5. Indinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 6. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of insulin aspart, insulin degludec, insulin detemir, insulin glargine, insulin glulisine, inhaled insulin, insulin lispro, and insulin NPH by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients, as estrogens may impair glucose tolerance. 7. Isavuconazonium sulfate increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 8. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. 9. Itraconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors like itraconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels. 10. Ivosidenib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy. 11. Ketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels. 12. Ethinyl estradiol decreases lamotrigine levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Combination oral contraceptives significantly reduce plasma concentrations of lamotrigine, likely due to induction of lamotrigine glucuronidation. Monitor closely. 13. Lapatinib levels or effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Larotrectinib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 15. Lemborexant levels or effects are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Lower nightly doses of lemborexant are recommended when coadministered with weak CYP3A4 inhibitors. Refer to the drug monograph for specific dosage adjustments. 16. Lenacapavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Lenacapavir, a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, may increase the risk of adverse reactions for CYP3A4 substrates initiated within nine months after the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir. 17. Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting BCRP. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Leniolisib may increase systemic exposure to BCRP substrates. 18. Lesinurad decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Additional nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended, as hormonal contraceptives alone may not be reliable. 19. Letrozole's effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Letrozole should not be used concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 20. Levofloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Levoketoconazole increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. CYP3A4 inhibitors like ketoconazole may elevate plasma hormone levels. 22. Ethinyl estradiol decreases liraglutide's effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may reduce the hypoglycemic effects of antidiabetics by impairing glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 23. Lixisenatide decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Oral contraceptives should be taken at least one hour before or 11 hours after lixisenatide administration. Monitor closely. 24. Lomitapide levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. The lomitapide dose should not exceed 30 mg/day. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Lonafarnib levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP3A4 metabolism inhibition. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration is unavoidable, reduce the lonafarnib dose and monitor for arrhythmias and other cardiac events. 26. Lonapegsomatropin's effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to growth hormone analogs. Higher growth hormone doses may be required. Monitor closely. 27. Lopinavir increases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Significant changes in estrogen plasma levels may occur, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Nonhormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. 28. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. Hormonal contraceptives may not be reliable during coadministration. 30. Lumequine decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Mavacamten decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Advise patients to use a contraceptive method unaffected by CYP450 enzyme induction or add nonhormonal contraception during coadministration and for four months after the last mavacamten dose. 32. Ethinyl estradiol decreases metformin's effects by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Metronidazole decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Metyrapone's effects are decreased by ethinyl estradiol through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinuation of estrogens may be advisable prior to and during metyrapone administration. 35. Mexiletine levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through CYP1A2 metabolism inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Midazolam levels are increased by ethinyl estradiol through decreased metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. 37. Mifepristone decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 38. Mineral oil decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Monitor closely. 39. Minocycline decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Mitotane decreases the levels of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of CYP3A4; dosage adjustments may be necessary. 41. Momelotinib increases the toxicity of ethinyl estradiol by competing for plasma protein binding. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Momelotinib may increase the risk of adverse reactions for BCRP substrates. 42. Moxifloxacin decreases the levels or effects of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to oral forms of the hormone and carries a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Mycophenolate decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol through an unknown mechanism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug.
